method.adjustment: re-weight recalled Harris and Trump voters so their two-party split equals the certified 2024 state result, other / non-voter groups fixed; 'cells' = the poll prints the race by recalled vote; 'approx' = shares only, group spread = median of the 'cells' polls
method.caveat: recalled-vote weighting has known biases: some 2024 voters misreport or forget (winner-recall drift towards Trump, non-recall among low-propensity Trump voters), 'shy' respondents, and midterm electorates differ from 2024's; many of these pollsters already weight on recalled vote, so a remaining gap can reflect the LV screen rather than the sample. Raw and adjusted are both shown; neither is a forecast.

history.question: did pollsters whose samples leaned D (proxy: their own mean signed error in earlier cycles, 538 raw_polls) miss more in the next cycle, and how much would removing that lean have fixed?
history.data: 538 raw_polls, Senate/governor general, final 21 days, D vs R; 2024 Senate/governor polls with pollster detail are not in any open-licence file we have (538 raw_polls ends with 2023; VoteHub serves only the current cycle), and no open archive of 2018-2022 recalled-2020-vote crosstabs exists
history.lean_rule: prior lean = pollster's mean error (absolute) or mean error minus its race's mean poll error (relative) in all earlier cycles, >= 5 polls, shrunk n/(n+10) before subtracting; d_lean > +1.0, r_lean < -1.0
